title: Ryser's Conjecture (Conjecture 1.1)
context_text: Attributed to Herbert Ryser and appearing in Henderson's 1971 PhD thesis, this conjecture generalises Kőnig's theorem to $r$-partite $r$-uniform hypergraphs. It was proved for $r=3$ by Aharoni in 2001 and remains open for all $r\geq 4$.
paper_contribution: The paper disproves Lovász's Conjecture 1.2 (which would have implied Ryser's conjecture via iterated matching-number reduction), thereby ruling out one proposed proof route; Ryser's conjecture itself remains open for $r\geq 4$.
paper_title: A Counterexample to a Conjecture of Lovász

title: Lovász Conjecture (Conjecture 1.2)
statement_text: Every $r$-partite, $r$-uniform hypergraph with at least one edge contains $r-1$ vertices whose deletion reduces the matching number.
context_text: Conjectured by Lovász in 1975 as a strengthening of Ryser's conjecture: if true, it would yield a vertex cover of size $(r-1)\nu(\mathcal{H})$ by iterative application. It was widely circulated through Füredi's 1988 survey on matchings and covers in hypergraphs.
paper_contribution: Disproves the conjecture for $r=3$ by exhibiting the line hypergraph of the Biggs-Smith graph (a cubic edge-transitive graph on 102 vertices) as an explicit counterexample; a second counterexample, the line hypergraph of the graph F168D on 168 vertices, is also identified.
paper_title: A Counterexample to a Conjecture of Lovász

title: Question 4.1
statement_text: Do there exist infinitely many $3$-edge colourable cubic graphs $G$ such that for all edges $(u,v),(x,y)\in E(G)$, $\alpha(G)=\alpha(G-\{u,v,x,y\})$?
context_text:
An $r$-partite $r$-uniform hypergraph has its vertex set partitioned into $r$ parts, each edge containing exactly one vertex of each part; a matching is a set of pairwise disjoint edges, $
u$ is the matching number and $	au$ the vertex cover number. Ryser conjectured $	au\le(r-1)
u$ for such hypergraphs (true for $r=2$ by Kőnig and $r=3$ by Aharoni, open for $r\ge4$), and Lovász (1975) conjectured the stronger statement that every such hypergraph with at least one edge has $r-1$ vertices whose deletion reduces the matching number. The line hypergraph $\mathcal{L}(G)$ of a graph $G$ has the edges of $G$ as vertices and, for each vertex $v$ of $G$, the set of edges incident to $v$ as an edge; $
u(\mathcal{L}(G))=\alpha(G)$, and if $G$ is $r$-regular and $r$-edge-colourable then $\mathcal{L}(G)$ is $r$-partite $r$-uniform. Deleting vertices $e_1,\dots,e_{k}$ of $\mathcal{L}(G)$ corresponds to forbidding the endpoints of these edges in an independent set of $G$. The authors disprove Lovász's conjecture for $r=3$: in the Biggs–Smith graph (a cubic distance-transitive graph on $102$ vertices), for every two edges $uv,xy$ there is a maximum independent set avoiding $u,v,x,y$. With a computer, the authors verified that the Biggs–Smith graph is the unique cubic edge-transitive graph on at most $166$ vertices with this property, that the $168$-vertex graph F168D of the Foster census also has it, that these are the only two cubic edge-transitive examples on at most $300$ vertices, and that no cubic graph on at most $20$ vertices has it. Each such $3$-edge-colourable cubic graph gives a counterexample to Lovász's conjecture; the question asks whether there are infinitely many.
paper_title: A Counterexample to a Conjecture of Lovász

title: Question 4.2
statement_text: Does there exist a $d$-regular $d$-edge colourable graph $G$ where $d\geq 4$ such that for all edges $(u_{1},v_{1}),\dots,(u_{d-1},v_{d-1})\in E(G)$, $\alpha(G)=\alpha(G-\{u_{1},\dots,u_{d-1},v_{1},\dots,v_{d-1}\})$?

title: Conjecture 4.3
statement_text: For every $r$-partite $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal{H}$ there exists some $k$ with $1\leq k\leq r-1$ such that $\mathcal{H}$ contains $k(r-1)$ vertices whose deletion reduces the matching number by at least $k$.

title: Question 4.4
statement_text: Is it true that if $\mathcal{L}$ is the line hypergraph of an $r$-regular $r$-edge colourable Cayley graph, then $\mathcal{L}$ contains $r-1$ vertices whose deletion reduces its matching number?
context_text:
An $r$-partite $r$-uniform hypergraph has its vertex set partitioned into $r$ parts, each edge containing exactly one vertex of each part; a matching is a set of pairwise disjoint edges, $

u$ for such hypergraphs (true for $r=2$ by Kőnig and $r=3$ by Aharoni, open for $r\ge4$), and Lovász (1975) conjectured the stronger statement that every such hypergraph with at least one edge has $r-1$ vertices whose deletion reduces the matching number. The authors note that symmetry clearly helps in identifying a counterexample, but it is not obvious why not being a Cayley graph should be beneficial, which motivates asking whether Lovász's conjecture holds for line hypergraphs of $r$-regular $r$-edge-colourable Cayley graphs.
